case.question: I fish for salmon from a boat. For this week, how good do you expect boat fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven: 1 (below average). Go here first.** Run 80-140 ft of water, with lines 50-90 ft down.
- **St. Joseph: 1 (below average).** Fish 75-100 ft of water if you go south. Use small rotators, flies, or meat rigs.
- **South Haven: 1 (below average).** Expect slow fishing around 100 ft of water, mostly on spoons.
- **Muskegon: 0 (slow).** Skip it this week unless you have new reports.
- Use glow spoons or meat rigs at Grand Haven. Bring spoons and small rotators or flies for the southern ports.

## Why

- Grand Haven is the only port where the latest report said boat action was "picking up slightly" (Grand Haven, 2025-07-09).
- Muskegon's latest report called boat fishing "on the slower side" (Muskegon, 2025-07-09).
- I'd expect the southern ports to stay around 1 because their most recent boat reports were slow overall, with only a few coho and Chinook caught (St. Joseph and South Haven, 2025-07-09).
- Past mid-summer weeks at about 72 F were mixed, usually rated 1 to 2, with some good weeks (find_similar_weeks, 2022-2024).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is 2025-07-09, six days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2025-07-09: boat, 80-140 ft of water, fish 50-90 ft down. Quality 1. "Salmon action started to pick up slightly for boat anglers." Glow spoons and meat rigs worked well.
- Muskegon, 2025-07-09: boat, 80-150 ft, fish 50-90 ft down. Quality 0. "Boats are finding salmon action to be on the slower side." Glow spoons and white flashers or flies.
- South Haven, 2025-07-09: boat, about 100 ft. Salmon quality 0 ("fishing slowed down"). Chinook and coho both quality 1, mostly spoons.
- St. Joseph, 2025-07-09: boat, 75-100 ft. Coho and Chinook both quality 1. "The best water appeared to be between 75 and 100 feet deep." Small rotators, flies, and meat rigs.
- The 2025-07-02 reports were also slow (quality 0-1) at all four ports.

**Past seasons (history, not current)**
- Similar water temperatures in past years produced mixed results. St. Joseph (2024-07-31) was rated 3 with fish "well beyond 120 feet deep," and Muskegon (2022-08-03) was rated 3 with fish 65-130 ft down. Those were good weeks, but the same weeks in other years were slow.

**Conditions now**
- The buoy summary for the week before today shows surface water at St. Joseph 76 F, South Haven 75 F, and Grand Haven/Muskegon 68 F (St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven, Muskegon; buoy summary).
- The tool labeled Grand Haven and Muskegon as a "possible upwelling (sharp drop)," but the reported change was +4 F, a rise. I'd treat that label as unreliable.
- No wind forecast or modeled cold-layer depth came back, so I couldn't check the weather for the coming days.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old (2025-07-09). Fishing may have changed since then.
- The conditions data was a backtest summary for the week before today, not live readings. The "upwelling" label conflicts with its own numbers.
- Ratings are my estimates from slow-to-fair reports. Reports say little about pier fishing, and nothing about this week's wind.
- If winds are strong, stay off the boat and check Grand Haven or Muskegon conditions before going out.

- Michigan DNR weekly report, 2025-07-09: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3e8bd76
- Michigan DNR weekly report, 2025-07-02: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3e7af82
